item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 15, 2026
item.description:
A heat advisory is in effect for Benton County until Saturday evening, with heat index values expected to reach 110 degrees.
NWS tulsa issues heat advisory for Benton county. A heat advisory has been issued for Benton County from August 14 at 10:49 PM CDT until August 16 at 8:00 PM CDT. Heat index values are expected to reach up to 110 degrees on Saturday, with higher values possible on Sunday.
On the Bentonville Utility Board agenda: Board to waive competitive bidding for 161 kV breakers. This would allow the Bentonville Utility Board to purchase four 161 kV breakers from GE Grid Solutions for $690,400.00 plus tax, without seeking other bids, for future substation projects. This decision is proposed due to market volatility and long lead times for these products.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider rezoning 405 NW 5th Street from suburban single-family to neighborhood node. This proposed change would allow for a mix of housing types and small-scale commercial uses at 405 NW 5th Street, potentially increasing density and local services in the area.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to reduce the prepared food and beverage tax rate. This proposed ordinance would decrease the tax you pay on prepared food and beverages from one percent to one-half of one percent. This means you would pay less tax when purchasing meals and drinks from local establishments.
On the Bentonville Public Art Advisory Board agenda: Board to provide feedback and a final recommendation for 'Near the Pitch'. This item involves a public art project that the board will discuss and potentially recommend for approval, which could lead to a new art installation in the city.
Bentonville Schools Board of education to meet on August 18. The Bentonville Schools Board of Education is scheduled to meet on August 18, 2026, at 5:30 PM at the Administration Building. The agenda includes a welcome, call to order, pledge, and approval of the agenda.
Circle of Life to purchase Washington Regional Hospice. Springdale-based Circle of Life will acquire Washington Regional Hospice and its Willard Walker Hospice Home in Fayetteville. Circle of Life is a nonprofit offering hospice and palliative care.
Walmart recalls tomato soup products due to listeria risk. Walmart stores in several states, including Arkansas, are recalling certain tomato soup products due to potential listeria contamination. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration reported the recall.
Fayetteville to close lane on Mission Boulevard for sidewalk construction. One lane of Mission Boulevard in Fayetteville will experience closures for new sidewalk construction beginning August 17. The closures are expected to last for several months.
Tyson Foods beef plant closures to impact communities. Tyson Foods' closure of two beef processing facilities and exploration of selling a third will create significant challenges and uncertainty in the affected communities. This information comes from beef organizations and local elected officials.
NorthWest Arkansas Community college receives $600,000 grant for mentorship. The Northwest Arkansas Community College's LIFE program has received a nearly $600,000 grant from the Walton Family Foundation. This funding will allow the program to expand its mentorship initiatives.
Fayetteville hosts bike helmet giveaway. The City of Fayetteville is hosting a bike helmet giveaway to promote cycling safety. This initiative aims to ensure residents can enjoy cycling safely.
Fayetteville Mayor Rawn appoints new c-suite members. Fayetteville Mayor Molly Rawn has appointed Jennifer Walker as the city’s chief of staff and Keith Macedo as chief information officer. These appointments are effective immediately.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 14, 2026
item.description:
A Heat Advisory has been issued for Benton County until Sunday at 8:00 PM CDT, with heat index values expected to reach 105 to 110 degrees.
Heat Advisory issued for Benton County. The National Weather Service in Tulsa, Oklahoma, has issued a Heat Advisory for Benton County, effective until Sunday, August 16, at 8:00 PM CDT. Heat index values are forecast to be between 105 and 110 degrees.
Bentonville Schools Board of education to meet August 18. The Bentonville Schools Board of Education will hold a meeting on August 18, 2026, at 5:30 PM at the Administration Building, 500 Tiger Blvd. The agenda includes a welcome, call to order, pledge, and approval of the agenda.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to hold a public hearing on rezoning 405 NW 5th Street from suburban single-family to neighborhood node. This proposed rezoning would change the allowed uses at 405 NW 5th Street from single-family homes to a neighborhood node, which typically allows for a mix of residential and small-scale commercial uses.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to reduce the prepared food and beverage tax rate. This proposed ordinance would decrease the tax you pay on prepared food and beverages from one percent to one-half of one percent. This means you would pay less tax when purchasing meals and drinks from local establishments.
On the Bentonville Public Art Advisory Board agenda: Board to provide feedback and final recommendation on 'Near the Pitch'. The board will discuss and potentially make a final decision on a public art project or initiative known as 'Near the Pitch'.
On the Rogers Water Utilities Commission agenda: Commission to approve Resolution 26-23 for purchasing plan review software. This resolution would authorize the purchase of software to assist with reviewing plans, potentially streamlining development processes related to water and sewer infrastructure.
Michaels to open new concept store in Rogers. Michaels is scheduled to open a new concept store location in Rogers.
Walmart AMP plans new buildings on property. City records indicate that the Walmart AMP concert venue is planning to add additional facilities to its property.
Alice L. Walton School of Medicine grows to nearly 100 students. The Alice L. Walton School of Medicine (AWSOM) in Bentonville has expanded its student body to 96, following the enrollment of its second class of 48 students in July.
NWACC and MIT collaborate on artificial intelligence curriculum. NorthWest Arkansas Community College (NWACC) and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) Pathways for AI Training and Hiring program met in Bentonville to explore developing an artificial intelligence curriculum.
Benton County to host annual passport Saturday event. Benton County will host its annual "Passport Saturday" event next month, allowing residents to apply for new passports without needing an appointment.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 13, 2026
item.description:
A heat advisory covering Benton County runs through Friday evening, with heat index values expected to reach 109 degrees.
Heat advisory issued for Benton County through Friday. The National Weather Service issued a heat advisory for Benton County and surrounding areas from Wednesday morning through Friday at 8 p.m., with heat index values forecast to reach 109 degrees.
Centerton approves $16.59 million bond for sewer system improvements. Centerton City Council approved a $16.59 million bond issue to fund improvements to the city's sewer collection system, which will allow additional development.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Rezone 405 NW 5th Street from single-family to neighborhood node. The property would shift from low-density suburban residential to a denser neighborhood node classification, allowing for different housing types and more concentrated development.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Propose changes to the Future Land Use Map. The map that guides long-term growth and development could be updated, affecting where different types of housing, businesses, and public uses are allowed across the city.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Update the community Code with ordinance amendments. The changes would revise existing development rules and standards, altering requirements for design, parking, and other site features for properties in the city.
Springdale City Council fills Ward 2 vacancy with former member. The Springdale City Council appointed a former council member to temporarily fill a Ward 2 vacancy for the next few months.
Herman's Ribhouse working to reopen in Fayetteville. Owner Nick Wright said work is underway to reopen the longtime Fayetteville restaurant.
Gentry Public Schools offering free lunches to all students. Starting this school year, Gentry Public Schools is providing lunch to all students at no charge.
Madison County forest gains permanent protection through conservation easement. The Northwest Arkansas Land Trust announced that a forested tract in Madison County will be permanently protected through a conservation easement.
Congressman Womack discusses airport loan application with federal official. Congressman Steve Womack and a U.S. Department of Transportation official met with Northwest Arkansas National Airport CEO Aaron Burkes to discuss the airport's application for a loan to fund a new concourse and rental car parking garage.
Ten tech companies pitch to investors at Fuse Demo Day. Ten Northwest Arkansas tech companies presented emerging technologies to investors, government stakeholders and economic developers at Fuse Ventures' Demo Day.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 12, 2026
item.description:
A Heat Advisory through August 16 is in effect for Benton County as officials highlight water conservation progress across Northwest Arkansas.
Heat Advisory issued through August 16 for Benton County. The National Weather Service has issued a Moderate Heat Advisory covering Benton County and multiple surrounding areas, active until August 13 at 1:15 AM.
Rogers voters to decide on issuing more than $450 million in bonds. Rogers voters will decide in November whether to allow the city to issue more than $450 million in bonds for capital improvement projects.
Centerton removes Flock Safety cameras. Centerton City Council voted to end the town's use of Flock Safety cameras, joining other Arkansas cities in removing the surveillance system.
Citizens Bank to open Fayetteville banking center. Batesville-based The Citizens Bank plans to open a new banking center at 1350 E. Joyce Blvd. in Fayetteville, moving beyond traditional banking models.
Walmart AMP plans two-story addition in Rogers. The Walmart Arkansas Music Pavilion in Rogers is planning a two-story front-of-house addition and a north addition, according to city plans.
Washington Regional hires chief medical informatics officer. Dr. Rowland “Todd” Stewart recently joined Washington Regional as vice president and the Fayetteville-based health system’s first chief medical informatics officer.
World champion squirrel cook off returns to Springdale. Hunters, outdoor enthusiasts and curious food lovers will converge on Springdale next month for a celebration of squirrel cooking.
Arkansas sees dip in new cyclosporiasis cases. The Arkansas Department of Health has identified 15 new cases of cyclosporiasis in a three-day span, more than half of which were in Northwest Arkansas.
Swarm Aero awarded $10 million government contract. Unmanned aircraft-maker Swarm Aero has secured a $10 million government contract that will be primarily executed at its new Fayetteville research and manufacturing facility.
Bentonville to close portion of southeast a street. The city is warning motorists to be aware of a street closing set to begin Thursday for water line work.
Two buildings demolished on college avenue in Fayetteville. Two buildings on one of Fayetteville's busiest streets have been razed to make way for a new bank.
Water conservation efforts show progress across NWA. After one day of suggested water savings, Scott Borman of the Benton Washington Regional Public Water Authority reported a noticeable difference in usage across the community.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 11, 2026
item.description:
A Heat Advisory is in effect for Benton County with heat index values up to 109 expected until 8:00 PM this evening.
Heat Advisory in effect until 8:00 PM this evening. The National Weather Service has issued a Heat Advisory for Benton County and surrounding areas due to heat index values reaching up to 109 degrees. The advisory is in effect until 8:00 PM CDT.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Approve a Planned Unit Development for properties at 902, 904, 906, 908, and 1002 SE 3rd Street. If approved, the specified properties would be developed under a Planned Unit Development, allowing a particular mixed-use design as outlined in the submitted plan.
On the Bentonville Finance Committee agenda: Authorization to accept grant for adaptive traffic signals. The council would approve taking a $700,000 grant to test AI-based traffic signals that adjust timing in real time, with a budget change needed to record and spend the grant money.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Proposed changes to the Future Land Use Map. Adopting the map changes would guide where different types of development are allowed across the city for years to come.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 10, 2026
item.description:
A heat advisory will affect Benton County through 8 p.m. today, with heat index values expected to reach 109 degrees.
Heat advisory in effect for Benton County through this evening. The National Weather Service has issued a heat advisory for Benton County and surrounding areas through 8 p.m. today, with heat index values expected to reach 109 degrees.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Approve a Planned Unit Development for properties at 902, 904, 906, 908, and 1002 SE 3rd Street. If approved, the detailed development plan for these parcels would be finalized, guiding how the site is built and used.
On the Bentonville Finance Committee agenda: Accept a grant to test adaptive traffic signals.. The city would receive a $700,000 grant to evaluate adaptive AI-based traffic signal technologies, leading to potential changes in how traffic lights operate in some areas.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Vacate a right of way and establish a drainage easement at Lot 13, Block 11 and Block 14 of Gilmore's Addition. The action would formally vacate the street right of way and create a drainage easement, affecting access and stormwater management for the area.
Bentonville council to consider items at Tuesday meetings. The Bentonville Finance Committee meets at 5 p.m. Tuesday, followed by a Combined Committee of the Whole and City Council meeting at 6 p.m. Agendas are available on the city portal.
Bella Vista holds short-term rental cap at 600 units. Following three months of City Council discussion, Bella Vista is maintaining its limit of 600 allowed short-term rentals after strong opposition to raising the number.
Rogers approves tree canopy restoration from 2024 tornado. Rogers City Council approved efforts to restore the city's tree canopy damaged in the 2024 tornado.
Samaritan Community Center names Gardner Andreas as executive director. Samaritan Community Center announced Gardner Andreas as its new executive director, with former executive director Debbie Rambo transitioning to a new role.
Swarm Aero receives $10 million in Air Force contracts. Swarm Aero, a drone company with manufacturing operations in Fayetteville, received $10 million in federal contracts to advance its high-rate manufacturing technology and produce aircraft components.
Flyway Brewing Company opens at Walmart Home Office. Flyway Brewing Company, a Little Rock-based microbrewery, officially opened Monday at Walmart's Home Office.
J.B. Hunt marks 65 years in business. J.B. Hunt Transport Services Inc. celebrated its 65th anniversary Monday by ringing the Nasdaq opening bell.
NWACC launches new dining service in student center. Northwest Arkansas Community College is launching a new on-campus dining service this week as students and staff return for the new semester.
Fayetteville schools, police urge caution as students return to class. Fayetteville Public Schools begin Tuesday, and police are urging all drivers in the city to slow down and pay closer attention as students return to class.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 9, 2026
item.description:
A heat advisory is in effect for Benton County until 8 p.m. Sunday, with heat index values expected to reach 108 degrees.
Heat advisory issued for Benton County through Sunday evening. The National Weather Service issued a heat advisory for Benton County from noon to 8 p.m. CDT on Sunday, with heat index values expected to reach 108 degrees. Heat-related illnesses are possible, especially for those not acclimated to the conditions.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Approve a Planned Unit Development for 1002 SE 3rd Street. The council would approve a PUD that allows more dense, mixed-use development at this corner, changing what can be built there.
On the Bentonville Finance Committee agenda: Authorization to accept grant for adaptive traffic signals. The council would approve taking a $700,000 grant to evaluate AI-based traffic signal technologies that could change how traffic is managed in the city.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Vacate a Right of Way and create a Drainage Easement at Gilmore's Addition. The ordinance would close this street segment and allow stormwater drainage infrastructure, affecting access and flooding management for nearby properties.
Bentonville council to consider finance and other matters at Monday meetings. The Bentonville Finance Committee meets Monday at 5 p.m., followed by a combined Committee of the Whole and City Council meeting at 6 p.m. Agendas have been published for both meetings.
Taziki's opens Rogers location. Taziki's Mediterranean Café opened at 1771 W. Pleasant Grove Road, Suite 104, in Rogers. The approximately 2,900-square-foot restaurant seats 85 guests and required $950,000 in investment.
Simmons Foods promotes Scott Salmon to chief commercial officer. Siloam Springs-based Simmons Foods promoted Scott Salmon, president of Simmons Pet Food, to the newly created role of chief commercial officer. Jacob Rogers will succeed Salmon in his previous position.
Walton Family Foundation grants $599,139 to NWACC for LIFE program. The Walton Family Foundation provided a $599,139 grant to Northwest Arkansas Community College to expand its Learning, Improvement, Fun and Empowerment program.
Jessica DeBari named executive director of Community Creative Center. Fayetteville artist Jessica DeBari has been appointed executive director of Community Creative Center, a Fayetteville-based nonprofit arts organization. She replaces Bryce Brisco, who stepped down in late July.
Tyson Foods board declares quarterly dividend of 51 cents per share. The Tyson Foods board of directors declared a quarterly dividend payment of 51 cents per share for Class A shareholders, payable on December 15.
Downtown Springdale Alliance hosts free picnic in the park series. Throughout August, the Downtown Springdale Alliance is hosting weekly Saturday events featuring food, music, and community gathering.
Terra Studios to host fourth annual Paws, Paint, & Play event in September. Terra Studios will host its fourth annual Paws, Paint, & Play event, a canine-friendly art park experience, on Sunday, September 6 from noon to 4 p.m.
Benton County study identifies site as candidate for possible nuclear development. A study presented to Arkansas lawmakers identified a site in Benton County as a candidate for possible future nuclear power development.
Benton County holds meeting on one-cent sales tax proposal. Benton County held an intergovernmental meeting to discuss a proposed one-cent sales tax.
